description: methodDetails.transactionVersions [0, 1]: an array of the integers 0 and 1 (the Wallet Standard vocabulary without "legacy"). The SDK's charge-request type parses it and re-encodes it unchanged, as integers; pins the canonical JSON.

spec.quote: Servers MUST accept every version they list, MUST reject any other version, and MUST NOT list 1 unless the enable_tx_v1 feature gate

description: methodDetails.transactionVersions [1]: a version-1-only server. The field round-trips through the SDK's charge-request type as written (not widened to the [0] default).

spec.quote: Servers MUST accept every version they list, MUST reject any other version, and MUST NOT list 1 unless the enable_tx_v1 feature gate

description: methodDetails.transactionVersions ["legacy"]: servers MUST NOT advertise legacy, so the value is outside the field's vocabulary and the SDK's charge-request type refuses it.

spec.quote: Legacy messages are not supported: servers MUST NOT advertise "legacy" and MUST reject a legacy message.

description: methodDetails.transactionVersions [0, 2]: each entry is the integer 0 or 1; version 2 does not exist, so no server can accept it and the request is refused (RULINGS T1).

expect.rejectReason: 2 is not a Solana message version

spec.quote: Servers MUST accept every version they list, MUST reject any other version, and MUST NOT list 1 unless the enable_tx_v1 feature gate

description: methodDetails.transactionVersions ["1"]: entries are integers, never strings (RULINGS T1).

spec.quote: Servers MUST accept every version they list, MUST reject any other version, and MUST NOT list 1 unless the enable_tx_v1 feature gate

description: methodDetails.transactionVersions 1: the field is an array, never a bare integer (RULINGS T1).

spec.quote: Servers MUST accept every version they list, MUST reject any other version, and MUST NOT list 1 unless the enable_tx_v1 feature gate

description: The challenge advertises [0, 1] and the signer is unrestricted: the client builds the highest advertised version, a version-1 message with the compute budget (computeUnitLimit set) in its header and no ComputeBudget instruction. The build judge compares the message version and header config with the kit's build.

spec.quote: Clients MUST build one of the advertised versions and SHOULD build the highest one their signer can produce.

description: The challenge advertises [1] only: the client MUST build version 1 (a version-0 build is not one of the advertised versions).

spec.quote: Clients MUST build one of the advertised versions and SHOULD build the highest one their signer can produce.

description: transactionVersions absent: it defaults to [0], so the client builds a version-0 message with the ComputeBudget prefix. A client that builds version 1 here sends a version the server never advertised.

spec.quote: Clients MUST build one of the advertised versions and SHOULD build the highest one their signer can produce.

description: The challenge advertises [0]: the client builds version 0 even though it could build version 1.

spec.quote: Clients MUST build one of the advertised versions and SHOULD build the highest one their signer can produce.

description: The challenge advertises [0, 1] but the signer signs version 0 only (input.signerMaxTransactionVersion = 0, e.g. a hardware wallet): the highest version the signer can produce is 0, and 0 is advertised.

spec.quote: Clients MUST build one of the advertised versions and SHOULD build the highest one their signer can produce.

description: The challenge advertises [1] only and the signer signs version 0 only: no advertised version is buildable, so the client MUST refuse up front rather than send version 0 (or fail at the device).

spec.quote: Clients MUST build one of the advertised versions and SHOULD build the highest one their signer can produce.

description: transactionVersions [] (present, empty): only an omitted field defaults to [0]. The client MUST build one of the advertised versions and none is advertised, so it refuses (RULINGS T2).

expect.rejectReason: an empty advertisement offers no version

spec.quote: Clients MUST build one of the advertised versions and SHOULD build the highest one their signer can produce.

description: transactionVersions [1, 1]: a repeated entry names the same version; the advertised set is {1} and the client builds version 1 (RULINGS T1).

spec.quote: Clients MUST build one of the advertised versions and SHOULD build the highest one their signer can produce.

description: Fee-sponsored challenge advertising [0, 1]: a version-1 message whose fee payer is feePayerKey, the client signing only as transfer authority (the sponsor slot stays empty; the build judge checks every slot).

spec.quote: When feePayer is true, the transaction MUST set the server's feePayerKey as fee payer, and the client signs only as transfer authority; the server adds the fee payer signature before broadcasting (see {{fee-sponsorship}}).

description: Native SOL charge advertising [0, 1]: a version-1 message carrying the System Program transfer, budget in the header.

spec.quote: Clients MUST build one of the advertised versions and SHOULD build the highest one their signer can produce.

description: Three 566-byte memos (externalId and two split memos) under [0, 1]: about 1.9 KB, which fits version 1's 4096-byte limit but not version 0's 1232. The client builds version 1.

spec.quote: A version-0 transaction MUST NOT exceed 1232 serialized bytes; a version-1 transaction MUST NOT exceed 4096 serialized bytes.

description: The challenge advertises [0, 1] and the credential is the kit's version-1 build: servers MUST accept every version they list.

spec.quote: Servers MUST accept every version they list, MUST reject any other version, and MUST NOT list 1 unless the enable_tx_v1 feature gate

description: The challenge advertises [1] only and the credential is a version-1 build.

spec.quote: Servers MUST accept every version they list, MUST reject any other version, and MUST NOT list 1 unless the enable_tx_v1 feature gate

description: The challenge carries no transactionVersions (so [0]) and the credential is a version-1 transaction (the kit's build for the same charge advertising [0, 1]). Rejected before any instruction is inspected: the transaction is otherwise valid.

spec.quote: Servers MUST reject a transaction whose version is not advertised, or which references an address lookup table, with the malformed-credential problem type, before inspecting any instruction.

description: The challenge advertises [0] explicitly and the credential is version 1.

spec.quote: Servers MUST reject a transaction whose version is not advertised, or which references an address lookup table, with the malformed-credential problem type, before inspecting any instruction.

description: The challenge advertises [1] only and the credential is a valid version-0 transaction (the kit's build for the same charge without the field). MUST reject any other version: version 0 is not implied.

spec.quote: Servers MUST reject a transaction whose version is not advertised, or which references an address lookup table, with the malformed-credential problem type, before inspecting any instruction.

description: The challenge advertises [0, 1] and the credential is a version-0 transaction: still accepted (positive control for the version-1-only and legacy rejects).

spec.quote: Servers MUST accept every version they list, MUST reject any other version, and MUST NOT list 1 unless the enable_tx_v1 feature gate

description: A legacy (unversioned) message with the kit's version-0 instructions, against a challenge advertising [0, 1]: servers MUST reject a legacy message. Pair: charge-verify-v0-with-v1-advertised-accept. Mutation: recompiled as a legacy message (compute budget as instructions).

spec.quote: Legacy messages are not supported: servers MUST NOT advertise "legacy" and MUST reject a legacy message.

description: A legacy message against a challenge with no transactionVersions: the default [0] does not admit legacy either. Pair: charge-verify-default-v0-accept. Mutation: recompiled as a legacy message (compute budget as instructions).

spec.quote: Legacy messages are not supported: servers MUST NOT advertise "legacy" and MUST reject a legacy message.

description: No transactionVersions and a version-0 credential: the default accepted set is [0].

spec.quote: Servers MUST accept every version they list, MUST reject any other version, and MUST NOT list 1 unless the enable_tx_v1 feature gate

description: A version-0 transaction whose recipient ATA is resolved through an address lookup table: the server cannot see the account in the static keys and MUST reject before inspecting any instruction. Pair: charge-verify-default-v0-accept. Mutation: transfer #0 destination resolved through an address lookup table.

spec.quote: Servers MUST reject a transaction whose version is not advertised, or which references an address lookup table, with the malformed-credential problem type, before inspecting any instruction.

description: The kit's version-1 build of the three-566-byte-memo charge, recompiled as version 0 (budget back into instructions): about 1.9 KB, over the version-0 limit of 1232 bytes, against a challenge advertising [0, 1]. Pair: charge-verify-v1-large-memos-accept. Mutation: recompiled as a version-0 message (compute budget as instructions).

spec.quote: A version-0 transaction MUST NOT exceed 1232 serialized bytes; a version-1 transaction MUST NOT exceed 4096 serialized bytes.

description: The same 1.9 KB charge as version 1: within the 4096-byte version-1 limit, accepted.

spec.quote: A version-0 transaction MUST NOT exceed 1232 serialized bytes; a version-1 transaction MUST NOT exceed 4096 serialized bytes.

description: A version-1 transaction that also carries a SetComputeUnitLimit instruction: ComputeBudget instructions have no effect under version 1, so a verifier that bounds them bounds nothing, and they MUST be rejected. Pair: charge-verify-v1-advertised-accept. Mutation: ComputeBudget instruction with data [2, 64, 13, 3, 0] added.

spec.quote: the transaction MUST NOT contain Compute Budget program instructions. They have no effect under version 1, and servers MUST reject them;

description: A version-1 header without computeUnitLimit: budgeted zero compute units, it cannot execute after the fee is charged. Pair: charge-verify-v1-advertised-accept. Mutation: version-1 header computeUnitLimit removed.

spec.quote: The transaction MUST set computeUnitLimit and loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit; a version-1 transaction that omits either is budgeted zero and cannot execute;

description: A version-1 header without loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit: budgeted zero bytes of account data, it fails at load time after the fee is charged. Pair: charge-verify-v1-advertised-accept. Mutation: version-1 header loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit removed.

spec.quote: The transaction MUST set computeUnitLimit and loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit; a version-1 transaction that omits either is budgeted zero and cannot execute;

description: Client-paid charge, version-1 header computeUnitLimit 200000 with priorityFee 1000000 lamports: 1000000 * 1000000 = 5000000 * 200000, exactly the 5000000 micro-lamport per-unit cap. Accepted (the cap is inclusive). Mutation: version-1 header priorityFee set to 1000000 lamports.

spec.quote: A server that caps the compute-unit price MUST evaluate priorityFee 1000000 <= maxPriceMicroLamports computeUnitLimit;

description: Client-paid charge, priorityFee 1000001 lamports over a 200000 unit limit: one lamport above priorityFee * 1000000 <= 5000000 * 200000. The total fee is normalised per unit, not compared with the per-unit cap directly. Mutation: version-1 header priorityFee set to 1000001 lamports.

spec.quote: A server that caps the compute-unit price MUST evaluate priorityFee 1000000 <= maxPriceMicroLamports computeUnitLimit;

description: Fee-sponsored charge (the sponsor caps the price at 10000 micro-lamports per unit), version-1 priorityFee 2000 lamports over 200000 units: 2000 * 1000000 = 10000 * 200000. Accepted. Mutation: version-1 header priorityFee set to 2000 lamports.

spec.quote: A server that caps the compute-unit price MUST evaluate priorityFee 1000000 <= maxPriceMicroLamports computeUnitLimit;

description: Fee-sponsored charge, priorityFee 2001 lamports over 200000 units: above the sponsor's 10000 micro-lamport per-unit cap. A sponsor that compares the lamport total with the per-unit cap (2001 < 10000) pays the client's priority fee. Mutation: version-1 header priorityFee set to 2001 lamports.

spec.quote: A server that caps the compute-unit price MUST evaluate priorityFee 1000000 <= maxPriceMicroLamports computeUnitLimit;

description: Fee-sponsored charge whose version-1 header lowers computeUnitLimit to 50 while keeping the 1-lamport priority fee: 1 * 1000000 > 10000 * 50, i.e. 20000 micro-lamports per unit. The total fee is under any per-unit number; only normalising by the declared limit exposes it. Mutation: version-1 header computeUnitLimit set to 50.

expect.rejectReason: 1 lamport over 50 units is 20000 micro-lamports per unit

spec.quote: A server that caps the compute-unit price MUST evaluate priorityFee 1000000 <= maxPriceMicroLamports computeUnitLimit;
